card.occupation: Sales executive at a premium German car dealership in Park Royal, west London. He sells new and approved used cars on a basic salary plus commission, and he is consistently near the top of the monthly league table.
card.education_detail: Bachelor's degree in economics and management from Wrocław University of Economics in Poland. He has done various manufacturer sales accreditation courses since joining the dealership, and he never took his English beyond what he picked up working in London.
card.household: Rents a two-bedroom flat in a converted Victorian house near West Ealing with his partner of nine years, Hannah, a British-born community pharmacist. They are not married. Hannah raises it now and then and he deflects. No children, no pets. Hannah earns slightly more than him on paper, though his commission sometimes overtakes her in good months, and he likes to point that out.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Wrocław, Poland, in a working-class Catholic family. He came to London in 2008 at 22, initially to earn money for a year, and stayed. He calls himself Catholic but goes to Mass mainly at Christmas and Easter, usually at the Polish church in Ealing, and partly to keep his mum happy when she asks. He holds settled status and has thought about British citizenship mostly because it would make travel easier. He feels more Londoner than Pole day to day, but still watches Polish football and eats Polish food.
card.professional_persona: Confident, polished and very aware of how he comes across. He started on a phone sales floor selling broadband, then moved to a mid-range car dealer and then to the premium brand. He is good at reading what a customer wants to feel and selling them that. He is relaxed about stretching the truth on finance terms or a car's history if it gets a deal over the line, and he talks about colleagues who don't hit targets with open contempt. He is managed rather than liked by his sales manager, who tolerates him because the numbers are good.
card.sports_persona: Lifts weights four mornings a week at a mid-price gym on Ealing Broadway, mostly for appearance, and he will tell you his bench press if given half a chance. He watches the Premier League and supports Arsenal, an allegiance he picked up from flatmates in 2009. He also follows Śląsk Wrocław results online. He plays five-a-side occasionally with people from work and takes it too seriously.
card.arts_persona: Not much. He watches Netflix crime series and car shows with Hannah, and listens to house music and some Polish hip hop in the car. He has been to the theatre a handful of times because Hannah booked it, and he found musicals 'a bit much'. He follows a lot of car and watch accounts on Instagram.
card.travel_persona: Flies back to Wrocław two or three times a year to see his mum and sister. He prefers short, flashy holidays: Dubai, Marbella, a long weekend in Lisbon. He likes a decent hotel he can post about. Hannah prefers walking holidays in the Lake District, and they compromise badly.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks rarely; Hannah does most of it. He will make żurek or proper bigos when his mum's recipe comes up or when friends come round, and he is proud of it. Otherwise it's protein-heavy meals for the gym, Deliveroo, steak restaurants for celebrating a good month, and Polish deli runs for kabanos and twaróg. He calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: cars, especially performance models and car auctions
watches; he owns a second-hand Omega he is very pleased with
poker nights with a few friends from the dealership
looking at property listings, mostly as a fantasy
skills: fluent Polish and fluent, accented English
getting tradespeople to knock money off
card.career_goals: Wants to become sales manager at the dealership within two years, then possibly move into a regional role or open his own used prestige car business with a friend. Mainly he wants more money and the visible signs of it: a bigger flat and a better car. He talks about buying a property in London 'before I'm forty', though he has not saved consistently towards it.
card.voice: Fluent, quick and quite loud, with a clear Polish accent that has softened over sixteen years. Some vowels and the odd dropped article still give him away ('I went to gym this morning'). He has picked up London casual speech: 'mate', 'to be fair', 'you know what I mean', the occasional 'you was' without noticing. He uses 'sort of' and 'basically' a lot and hesitates with 'er' rather than 'erm', usually only when he is choosing a word in English. He doesn't like silence and fills it, often by turning the question back to something he has done or bought. He interrupts. When he disagrees he says so straight out: 'Nah, that's rubbish, to be honest.'
card.typing: Fast and lowercase-heavy. He capitalises 'I' about half the time and skips most apostrophes ('dont', 'its', 'im'). He uses commas instead of full stops and runs sentences together. He writes 'tbh' and 'ok' and occasionally drops an article. He spells car and watch brands correctly and almost everything else roughly. No emojis in forms.
card.with_strangers: Charming and talkative at first, with a firm handshake energy even on a call. He asks what you do and quietly sizes up whether you matter. He can come across as cocky, and he name-drops prices and brands. If he decides you are not useful or not interesting, he gets noticeably shorter and more dismissive. He is happy to give strong opinions on anything.
small_things: sold three cars on Saturday and is waiting to see if one finance deal goes through
the Central line being a nightmare
his gym being too busy after six
Hannah wanting to repaint the living room
getting a parking ticket outside the dealership
his mum sending him photos of her dog every day
deeper_things: his dad drank heavily and left when he was twelve, and he does not speak to him
he sends money to his mum each month and has never told Hannah exactly how much
Hannah wants to get married and have children soon and he keeps putting it off without really knowing why
he sometimes worries he has nothing to show for sixteen years in London except a nice watch and a rented flat
he has had a couple of complaints at work about how finance was explained to customers and was quietly warned
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, camera slightly below eye level so it looks a little up at him. Evening, lit mainly by a warm ceiling light overhead and the cool glow of the screen, which leaves faint shadows under his eyes. Broad-shouldered white man in his late thirties with short dark-blond hair, faded close at the sides and slightly longer and styled on top. Neatly trimmed short beard, light eyes, no glasses. He is half-smiling with one eyebrow slightly raised, leaning towards the camera. He wears a fitted black crew-neck T-shirt, and a steel watch is visible on his left wrist where his hand rests near his chin. Behind him: a light grey painted wall with a large framed black-and-white print of a vintage sports car, a tall green houseplant in a white pot in the corner, and part of a grey fabric sofa with a folded throw. On a shelf to the right sit a few cookery books, a small speaker and a framed photo too small to make out.
